text: There are now more seniors living in Toronto than children. The growth in the seniors population is expected to accelerate in coming years. By 2031, one quarter of the City's population will be over the age of 60. The City recognizes that there are policy, service and resource implications to this significant demographic shift. At the same time, the increased life expectancy is a triumph and we all benefit from the energy, resilience and contribution of Toronto seniors. In 2013, City Council approved the Toronto Seniors Strategy Version 1.0. As a result of Version 1.0 and the progress of implementation, in 2016 Toronto was recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a Global Age-Friendly City.
